instruction: Make more_itertools.numeric_range equality and hashing follow the built-in range: two numeric_range objects are equal when they describe the same sequence, that is, they have the same length and, when non-empty, the same first value and, when longer than one, the same step. So numeric_range(2, 3, 1) == numeric_range(2, 3, 5) (both are just [2]), numeric_range(0, 5, 2) == numeric_range(0, 6, 2), every empty numeric_range equals every other, and numeric_range(0, 5, 2) != numeric_range(0, 7, 2). This holds for int, float, Decimal, Fraction and datetime/timedelta ranges. Equal ranges must have equal hashes, and the hash should still tell unequal ranges apart as a good hash does. A numeric_range is equal to itself and never equal to an object of another type (numeric_range(7.0) != 1, != 'abc').
